Published online:
    September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: US, with material coverage of Asia-Pacific, Europe, Middle East)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    Surging oil prices driven by Middle East conflict (US-Iran exchanges, Houthi seizure of Yemen's Mocha port, Strait of Hormuz disruptions) are stoking global inflation fears and triggering a broad bond selloff. US 10-year yields are approaching the critical 5% threshold, 30-year yields hit 19-year highs, and markets are pricing ~70% probability of a Fed rate hike. JPMorgan expects 8 of 9 DM central banks to tighten before year-end. Asian equities sold off sharply; gold and the USD firmed. August CPI data (due same day) is the near-term pivot point for Fed decision-making.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (US yields and Fed rate path are the central thread, with oil/geopolitics as the driver)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly centered on the case for a Fed hike)
Probability of increase: 70% (explicitly cited market pricing)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (holding is not a featured scenario; it is the implicit alternative if CPI surprises to the downside)
Probability of holding: 30%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (cuts are entirely absent from the narrative)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (Distinctly hawkish — yields near multi-year highs, ~70% market-implied hike probability, sticky PPI, oil-driven inflation pressure, and JPMorgan calling for broad DM tightening all point firmly in one direction; the only mild offset is S&P futures +0.2% and a slightly softening oil price intraday)
